THE GUIDE

How to choose the right digital marketing agency in Bangalore.

Quick answer

Pick the agency that can show you the actual numbers behind a past result, not just the result — and one that runs your channels as one connected system instead of separate vendors billing you for the same customer twice.

  • Case studies with real numbers — traffic, cost per lead, revenue, not just "we grew their Instagram."
  • One team, not five vendors — your web dev, SEO and ads should share one strategy, not compete for credit.
  • A reporting cadence you actually understand — plain numbers on a schedule, not a 40-slide deck once a quarter.
  • Someone who'll tell you no — a good agency turns down work that won't move your numbers.
Get a free consultation

Start with outcomes, not deliverables.

Most pitches lead with what an agency does — "we build websites, run ads, write content." What actually matters is what happens to your numbers after. Ask any shortlisted agency to walk you through one client, start to finish: where the metrics stood before, what changed, and how long it took. If they can't do that without pulling up a case study PDF, they probably haven't done the work themselves.

Find out who's actually doing the work.

A lot of agencies sell you a senior strategist in the pitch and hand you off to a junior team the week after signing. Ask directly who will be on your account day to day, and how much of the delivery is in-house versus subcontracted. DG5 keeps every discipline — web, SEO, ads, ecommerce, automation — under one roof specifically so nothing gets lost in a handoff between agencies.

Match the agency to your growth stage.

An early-stage brand validating demand needs fast, cheap experiments — a landing page and a performance ads sprint, not a six-month SEO retainer. An established brand with existing traffic needs the opposite: compounding, structural work like technical SEO and marketing automation. The right agency asks about your stage before they pitch you a package.

Price the relationship, not the invoice.

The cheapest quote is rarely the cheapest outcome once you count the cost of a rebuild in eight months, or a campaign that never got past setup. Ask what happens if the first approach doesn't work — a good agency has already thought about it.
